title: Bootstrapping Classical Systems with Quenched Disorder
authors: Minjae Cho, Yaprak Önder, Eslam Khalaf, Michael G. Scheer
abstract: We introduce a bootstrap method for deriving bounds on disorder-averaged observables in classical statistical systems with quenched disorder. The three main ingredients of the bootstrap are the positivity of ensembles of probability measures, disorder-averaged equations of motion, and explicit expectation values of random coupling variables. Together, these ingredients lead to a linear programming problem over the space of disorder averages. By further employing the positivity of the two-replica Gram matrix, we also formulate a semidefinite programming problem that produces bounds on two-replica correlators. We demonstrate the method using two examples: the two-dimensional random site-diluted Ising model and the one-dimensional disordered contact process. For the latter example, the bootstrap bounds exhibit a region of multiple kinks that we relate to the Griffiths region, whose finite-size scaling analysis yields a typical correlation length exponent in good numerical agreement with the known value.
summary: This work introduces a powerful bootstrap framework using linear and semidefinite programming to derive rigorous bounds on observables in disordered classical statistical systems. By applying this to models like the random Ising model, the authors successfully analyze complex phenomena such as the Griffiths region. It provides a mathematically rigorous approach to tackling the notoriously difficult problem of quenched disorder.
main_problem: The paper develops a bootstrap method to derive rigorous mathematical bounds on disorder-averaged observables in classical statistical systems subjected to quenched disorder.
main_result: The method successfully applies to models like the random site-diluted Ising model and the disordered contact process, yielding bounds that can be analyzed for critical behavior, such as identifying the Griffiths region.
method: The core method involves reformulating the constraints imposed by the disorder average into a sequence of linear programming (LP) and semidefinite programming (SDP) problems.
model_or_system: The study focuses on classical statistical systems with quenched disorder, exemplified by the two-dimensional random site-diluted Ising model and the one-dimensional disordered contact process. The physics is governed by disorder-averaged Hamiltonians and probability measures.
key_observables: Disorder-averaged magnetization, nearest-neighbor correlators, two-replica correlators, and probabilities $P_1, P_2, P_3$ exhibiting kinks.
important_parameters: The disorder concentration parameter ($p$), temperature/inverse temperature ($ eta$), and lattice size ($L$) are crucial parameters defining the phase diagram and scaling behavior.
main_assumptions: The method relies on the positivity of probability measures, the existence of disorder averages, and the ability to formulate constraints as linear/semidefinite inequalities.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the transition of probabilities across 'kinks' in the phase diagram and compare bootstrap bounds (with and without specific inequalities) against expected theoretical values.
paper_structure: The paper builds the framework by defining the mathematical constraints (positivity, equations of motion) and then applying this framework to specific models (RSIM, DCP) to derive bounds and analyze critical phenomena like the Griffiths region.
why_interesting: The rigorous mathematical techniques developed (LP/SDP bounds) provide powerful, non-perturbative tools to analyze complex, disordered many-body systems, which is a major challenge in modern statistical physics.
